direction: Autoregressive emulator on Lorenz-96. Two-scale Lorenz-96 (36 slow variables) integrated in NumPy as the truth. Train a 1D CNN one-step emulator on the slow variables with one-step versus multi-step rollout loss. Measure RMSE and anomaly correlation versus lead time against persistence and climatology, and long-run stability and climatological variance. Keep it a small CPU study with reimplemented baselines, at least 5 seeds where cheap, and report negative or mixed results plainly.

notes.note: K=2 sweep, noise ablation, ntrain sweep

decisions.decision: Training budget fixed at 1500 Adam steps x batch 32 for every K (multi-step costs K times more compute per step, noted); lr tuned on validation RMSE at 1 time unit with a dedicated seed 100, lr in {1e-3,3e-3} for K=1 and K=4. Method display name is CNN K=4 (multi-step), CNN K=1 is the one-step reference baseline. Fast variables are never shown to the emulator.

lr=3e-3 chosen for all CNN variants: on the validation split (seed 100) it beat 1e-3 for both K=1 and K=4 on val_rmse_t10 (0.40 vs 0.51; 0.39 vs 0.48) and val_rmse_t20. No tuning of baselines is possible (persistence/climatology have no parameters; linear stencil is closed-form with fixed ridge 1e-3).
